dossier.name: histor
dossier.purpose: Self-described in its user-agent as "histor/0.1.0" making read-only MCP probes (initialize + tools/list only). No operator page or public documentation could be found as of 2026-10-23.
dossier.robots_note: A site histor.dev ('The evidence layer for autonomous AI', HTTPS receipts for agents) exists, but no page found ties it to this UA; not attributed.

why_it_matters.text: Read-only MCP handshake probe; shows something is cataloguing or witnessing our tool list.

matching.rule: Reduce each agent_days label to a token: for labels starting with Mozilla/ take the product after 'compatible;', else a versioned crawler token such as 'FooBot/1.0' (a truncated 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 7.0;) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile' prefix logged before 23 Oct 2026 is PetalBot; anything else is unidentified-android, unidentified-linux-chrome or unidentified-browser); otherwise take the text before the first '/', '(' or ';' and drop a trailing ' token probe'. Lowercase it. A dossier owns the tokens in its aliases.

observed_baseline.note: Refreshed daily in production from the live aggregates (dated by as_of). For current numbers aggregate live_sources.history agent_days by matching.aliases.

dossier.identity_note: A family name is what a client claims in its user agent. It is verified only when its request came from the operator's published IP ranges or passed forward-confirmed reverse DNS, as reported per family in /crawler-journeys.json. Anyone can claim any name.

privacy.raw_user_agents: not_output (labels are sanitized; URLs inside them are redacted)

history_window.coverage_rule: A day bucket is replaced only by a report whose log window covers more of that UTC day; a closed day never shrinks. complete = the log window spans the whole UTC day; in_progress = the day has not ended; partial = log rotation cut the day; unknown = legacy bucket written before coverage tracking.

notes: Generated from sanitized aggregate traffic reports, not raw logs.
History keeps daily count buckets and agent first-seen dates only.
New Runtime monitoring checks and generic utility clients stay separated from public bot totals.
Scanner noise is shown as named scanner families when available, otherwise grouped by probe type.
Each bucket carries coverage: the part of its UTC day the source access logs spanned. Only complete buckets are full-day counts.

Sort | Most requests | Last seen

Perplexity | PerplexityBot surfaces and links websites in Perplexity search results and is not used to crawl content for AI foundation models. The separate Perplexity-User fetcher opens pages on user request to answer a question and link the page. | search index

Parallel Web Systems | Parallel Web Systems' crawler; it collects publicly available web content to build and maintain Parallel's search index (Parallel sells web search/research APIs for AI agents). A separate Shap-User agent handles user-triggered fetches and does not crawl automatically. | search index

Keenable | Builds and maintains the Keenable search index, which answers queries from AI agents and applications and cites source pages with links. A separate Keenable-User agent fetches single pages on behalf of a person or their agent. | search index

xAI (unconfirmed; UA claims x.ai) | User agents that claim to be xAI (GrokBot/1.0, xAI-SearchBot/1.0 with +https://x.ai). Third-party directories describe xAI-SearchBot as fetching/indexing pages for Grok search and answers; GrokBot's purpose is undisclosed. xAI publishes no crawler documentation. | unknown
Google | Google crawler that performs crawls requested by site owners to build Vertex AI Agents; Google says it has no effect on Google Search or other products. | research
Meta | Fetches individual links at a user's request, including for agentic AI tasks in Meta AI products. | live answer fetch
14 | Collect pages for model training or open web datasets, plus the robots.txt control tokens that govern that use. | Meta-ExternalAgent

Reflection AI | Reflection AI's web crawler. It visits publicly available web pages to help build and improve the company's (open) AI models; it is currently the only user agent Reflection AI crawls with. | model training

Amazon | Amazon crawler used to improve Amazon products and services; Amazon states its data may be used to train Amazon AI models. Related agents: Amzn-SearchBot (search, e.g. Alexa; no AI training) and Amzn-User (live user-request fetches). | model training

Google | Not a crawler: a standalone robots.txt product token that lets publishers control whether content crawled by Google may be used to train future Gemini models and for grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI. It has no separate HTTP user-agent string; crawling uses existing Google user agents. | model training

ByteDance | ByteDance crawler described by secondary sources as an AI data scraper, allegedly used to build training data for ByteDance LLMs such as Doubao. No operator documentation was opened. | model training
Apple | Secondary user agent that does not crawl; it only governs whether data already crawled by Applebot may be used to train Apple's foundation models. | model training

Huawei (Petal Search) | Huawei's crawler for the Petal Search engine; directories also say it supplies content recommendations for Huawei Assistant and other Huawei AI services. It crawls mostly with a mobile user agent that looks like Chrome on Android 7.0 and names itself only at the end ('compatible; PetalBot'). Official page (webmaster.petalsearch.com/site/petalbot) is JS-only and could not be read. | search index

LohiSoft s.r.o. | Builds LohiSoft's own search index from page titles, meta descriptions, h1-h3 headings, URLs and inbound link text (not page bodies), at most 20 pages per site. The operator states it does not collect AI training data or republish content. | search index

Ora | Ora's on-demand scanner that scores how ready a website is for AI agents. When someone requests a score for a domain it fetches robots.txt, llms.txt, OpenAPI specs, MCP manifests, structured data and /.well-known/poppy.json in a bounded burst; during a scan it also requests the homepage under other crawlers' UAs (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot). | monitoring
